rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consolidated verdict; four facets checked against `bosser-strategy:content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md` §§ Mood arc, M4 in detail, M5 in detail. (a) BIG IDEA FIDELITY — the strategy doc's M4 spirit is 'M4 doesn't prepare, it tests', while line 4 leads 'Prep your first long session.' That register gap is real and is the closest this file comes to a §4 finding; it is NOT filed, because maintainer 97 carries a dated accept-note that anticipates this exact judge ('A `strategy` judge scoring `check_strategy_tie_in.md` §1 reads the first clause as prep-register ... Do not rewrite the Big Idea to resolve the judge'), names the experiment framing as living in the second sentence, names the trainer reframe that catches the drift in the room (121), and names the firing condition tracked in `pre-cohort-todos.md`. Per the dispatch preamble, an existing accept-note on the passage means it is not flagged at all. (b) NO FRONT-RUN — M5 owns the naming of Ronacher's three-pattern from felt evidence. This file names its three pieces only by ABSENCE and without attribution: 23, 'no plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact', and 51, 'The task went out un-packaged: no plan file, no verifier, no reference artefact.' That is the strategy doc's own baseline wording ('Send off, un-packaged ... do not add a new long-run recipe before the baseline runs'); the reveal M5 owns is each piece EARNING its name against a specific failure, and nothing here teaches what any of the three does or why. Maintainer 105 further records that the reassurance which DID pre-announce M5's job was cut for exactly this reason. (c) MOOD DOESN'T RESOLVE EARLY — the Horthy provocation at 16 is left unanswered by design (105), Key Concepts (50-53) recap the run without resolving it, and `## Bring to Module 5` (67) hands a trace forward rather than a conclusion. (d) MODULE-TO-MODULE ARC — line 91, 'The next module opens with what came back', against the strategy doc's 'M5 opens with the return.' rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Leap test present at 153-156, three items, each with a named verb and a 'Falsifiable:' clause naming the evidence a working engineer could point at by Monday: (1) 'git log shows a `<prefix>/<slug>` branch with a "starting point" commit message before the agent's first task-execution commit'; (2) 'scrollback of a long-running task shows a manual stop with a one-line note about what wobbled'; (3) 'pre-task observations diff shows two-or-three new observations or rules tied to the task at hand, not a comprehensive sweep'. Read in isolation, each is decidable — the engineer opens git log, opens the scrollback, opens the diff. Closest to a competency claim: item 2's 'names the failure mode in writing', which stays inside because the falsifier pins it to a written artefact with a stated ceiling (<=20 minutes) rather than to a quality of the naming. TEACHING MOMENT LANDS (no check_strategy_tie_in rule_index; recorded here per the template). The named teaching moment is the un-packaged send-off producing a readable-but-underdelivering result that M5 diagnoses. It cannot be skipped by persona-skill variation, because it is not a comprehension beat: the student dispatches a real task on their own repo and the result is whatever it is. The two failure directions are both caught by the body rather than by trainer luck — a student who wants to package first meets 'no plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact' in the LO (23) and again in Key Concepts (51), and a student whose run stalls meets 'A stopped session counts; the trace is the artefact' (67) and 'Traces are data' (52). A stronger engineer landing a cleaner run still carries a trace to read, which is the only thing M5 requires.
